interfaces.name: Web application
interfaces.classification_rationale: Actions are expressed by manipulating views, forms, and controls of a persistent, navigable workspace representation.

provenance.evidence: First-party web client listed among Clockify apps.
Help center documents web/app surfaces for tracking time.

interfaces.name: Desktop application
interfaces.classification_rationale: Native desktop client operated through affordance manipulation over a navigable local representation, with offline mode and auto tracker.

provenance.evidence: Windows, Mac, and Linux clients listed as first-party apps.
Mac desktop app published by CAKE.com Inc.

interfaces.name: Mobile application
interfaces.classification_rationale: Native mobile client operated through affordance manipulation of the Clockify workspace.

provenance.evidence: Android and iOS clients listed as first-party apps.
Android app published by Cake.com Inc.

interfaces.name: Browser extension
interfaces.classification_rationale: First-party extension exposing a popup and an injected timer control the user operates directly; the primitive is manipulation of presented controls, not structured operation invocation.

provenance.evidence: Documents the first-party browser extension, its timer controls, reminders, and settings.

interfaces.name: Kiosk
interfaces.classification_rationale: Shared-device surface where limited users clock in via PIN, QR code, or photo capture; distinct contract but the same affordance-manipulation primitive.

provenance.evidence: Documents the kiosk opened via a browser link with PIN/QR/photo clock-in for limited members.

interfaces.name: REST API
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes provider-defined operations over resources through structured HTTP requests; report endpoints share the same style and auth and are the same interface.

provenance.evidence: Official API docs: base URL api.clockify.me/api/v1, X-Api-Key auth, operations over workspaces, projects, time entries, reports, and webhook management.

interfaces.name: Webhooks
interfaces.technology: Provider-initiated HTTP callbacks to a subscriber endpoint
interfaces.classification_rationale: The service initiates the interaction when subscribed events occur and delivers to a consumer-controlled endpoint.

provenance.evidence: Webhooks section: real-time notifications sent to your endpoint on events such as starting a timer or deleting a time entry.

interfaces.name: MCP server
interfaces.classification_rationale: First-party MCP endpoint exposing discoverable tools, prompts, and resources selected by an AI agent by goal; capability discovery and selection are part of the contract, so the MCP boundary case makes it Agentic rather than Programmatic.

provenance.evidence: Official help page documenting the Clockify MCP endpoint, its tools, prompts, and resources; labeled COMING SOON as of 2026-09-22 (preview).

access_mechanism_ledger.detail: No provider-shipped Clockify CLI or TUI; the CLIs in the MCP docs are third-party AI agents used to reach the MCP server.
Folded into REST API: same REST style and X-Api-Key auth.
No first-party natural-language assistant inside Clockify; NL interaction occurs in external agents consuming the MCP interface.

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: Integrations index (Jira, QuickBooks, Xero, Zapier, Make, Pipedream, 2,900+ apps)
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Third-party integrations/connectors that consume the REST API, webhooks, or the extension.
Cross-product integration delivered via API/webhooks, not a distinct Clockify interface.
SDKs and wrappers are not interfaces; also unofficial.
